setting: You are all members of a monthly book club that meets in a café in Grünerløkka, Oslo, and uses this group chat to pick books and confirm meetings. You have known each other for about three years, since the club began, and have shared dinners and walks outside the meetings. You know each other's jobs, rough family situations and reading tastes, but not much about each other's private troubles.
opener: Proposing the next book and asking who can host the January meeting.

Ingrid.knows: You know Mateo as a lively talker who always has a strong opinion on the book, Saskia as a nurse who joined two years ago and is very direct, Tobias as a quiet and reliable IT consultant who lives with Saskia, and Lena as a warm, curious friend who joined the club last year.
Ingrid.like: You are organised and warm, and you like keeping things moving.
Ingrid.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to set dates or ask for book choices.
Ingrid.style: You use few emoji and only standard spelling.

Mateo.knows: You know Ingrid as the club's organiser who keeps everyone on track, Saskia as a sharp nurse who will argue a point until it is settled, Tobias as a calm friend who rarely says much but is always listening, and Lena as a thoughtful newcomer who often notices things others miss.
Mateo.like: You are enthusiastic and talkative, and you get excited about ideas.
Mateo.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually to share thoughts on the book or suggest something.
Mateo.style: You use the occasional emoji and write in full sentences.

Saskia.knows: You know Ingrid as the organiser who is always fair, Mateo as an enthusiast who gets carried away but means well, Tobias as your partner who is quiet and dependable, and Lena as a friend you are still getting to know.
Saskia.like: You are direct and honest, and you say what you think without fuss.
Saskia.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you have an opinion on the book or need to change plans.
Saskia.style: You rarely use emoji and keep messages short.

Tobias.knows: You know Ingrid as the organiser you have known since the club started, Mateo as a friend who talks more than anyone, Saskia as your partner who speaks her mind, and Lena as a newer member you like having around.
Tobias.like: You are calm and dependable, and you rarely say more than you need to.
Tobias.texts: You message the group rarely, mostly to answer a direct question or confirm you can come.
Tobias.style: You almost never use emoji and use no abbreviations.

Lena.knows: You know Ingrid as the warm organiser who welcomed you to the club, Mateo as a talkative guy who is fun to argue with, Saskia as a friend who is blunt but kind, and Tobias as a quiet man who always seems to have thought things through.
Lena.like: You are curious and friendly, and you like asking questions.
Lena.texts: You message the group fairly often, usually with questions or reactions to what others say.
Lena.style: You use a few emoji and some casual abbreviations like "tbh".

private_lines.Ingrid: You work as a secondary school teacher in Oslo and live alone in a flat in Sagene. Your days are full of marking and lessons, and you usually read in the evenings before bed.
private_lines.Mateo: You work as a software developer in Oslo and live alone in a rented flat in Grünerløkka. You work from home most days, go running after work, and spend a lot of your free time reading.
private_lines.Saskia: You work as a nurse on shifts at a hospital in Oslo and live with Tobias in an apartment in Majorstuen. Your shifts vary, so your days can be early starts or late nights, and you try to read on your days off.
private_lines.Tobias: You work as an IT consultant, often on client sites or from home in your flat in Majorstuen with Saskia. You keep a fairly regular routine, with work during the day and a walk or a book in the evenings.
private_lines.Lena: You work as a graphic designer for a small studio in Oslo and live with a flatmate in a shared flat in Grünerløkka. You often work on a laptop at home, go to the gym a few times a week, and read on the tram.

text: Morning all. Next book for January: I'd like to propose Stoner by John Williams. Short, a lot to argue about. Thoughts?
Oh yes, Stoner. I haven't read it since university and I think I'd get something different out of it now. Count me in.
It's sad. Fine by me though.
I haven't read it! Is it very depressing? I read a lot of Norwegian stuff lately and I need a break from grief
It is depressing. Beautifully so. Worth it
Lena, it's sad but not miserable. Mostly it's about a man who doesn't say much and it's hard not to take it personally.
That's the whole book
Also: who can host the January meeting? Café is closed the week after New Year so I'd like to try a flat this time. Doesn't need to be big, we'd be 5 plus whoever.
I can, though my place is small. Do we have a limit? I have a decent kettle and that's about it
Kettle is fine Mateo
I could but my flatmate has a thing with people in the kitchen. I'd ask her first
Ours works. Saskia's on shifts that week, I'll check.
Thank you Tobias. Let me know by Friday if you can.
Stoner's fine. Tell Mateo to stop calling it beautiful, it's not a holiday read
I did not say holiday. I said beautiful, which is a different thing 🙂
Ok
Has anyone got a copy with the old cover? The library one has the new one and I can't stand it
I have one somewhere, I'll look tomorrow. Honestly I'm not sure I could find anything in my flat
Thank you!
Just finished chapter 3 for the third time because I keep thinking about the scene with the dean. Anyone else feel like the book is quietly furious?
Mateo, I'm marking. Ask me Thursday.
Fair enough
I'm not going to sleep, sorry. Reading on the tram tomorrow is going to be a nightmare
Found it. Old cover, spine cracked, and someone's pencil notes in the margins which I'm fairly sure are mine from 2004. I'll bring it Thursday if you still want it
You're a saint. Pencil is fine, I'll take it with the notes
Some of the notes are just "sad" with an arrow
Break. Tobias says he'll check the flat but he's sure it's fine. I'm on nights 4 to 8 Jan, so that's a no for me that week
Not that I'm hosting anything
You're not hosting. You're coming
Ok
Saskia, thanks. Tobias, can you confirm when you've checked? Friday is still the deadline
Can do the 15th. Saskia's off that day
Perfect. Thank you
The 15th is a Thursday. Good, I'll be there. Kettle's ready
Good. Don't make me eat anything with lentils
Nobody has ever made lentils for the club
Someone will
15th is fine for me. I'll ask Mette about the kitchen anyway, she's the one who'd notice
Lovely. The 15th at Tobias and Saskia's, confirmed. Mateo, I'll give you my view on the dean on Thursday
Still think the dean scene is the worst thing in the book. Everyone just stands there
It's not furious. It's tired
A tired fury. That's what I said
Tram tomorrow. Where's the department meeting, is it chapter 3 or 4? I can't remember
Chapter 4, opening. You'll hate it
Already do
Ok. Going to try properly this time
Still awake. This is a bad habit
Up. Tram in ten. Didn't read, just lay there after the alarm
Stoner is on the hall table, right by the door so I can't forget it
Pencil and all
Thank you. Did you underline the bit about the daughter or was that someone else
Probably me. I underlined everything in 2004
Morning. Mateo, Thursday, I'll give you my view on the dean then. Lena, the library copy is due back Friday so keep that one out of the bag
Nights from tonight. If anyone asks about the sofa, ask Tobias. I haven't seen it since August
Tobias, is the sofa a problem?
Not a problem. Seats three and a half. We'll put the good chair next to it
Three and a half is the most honest thing anyone has said about a sofa in this group 🙂
Ok
Good. That's six with the chair
Mette says the kitchen is fine if we don't do anything with the oven. Not sure what she thinks we'd do with the oven
Lentils
Nobody mention lentils
Ran up Akerselva in the rain. Still thinking about the dean. Nobody in that book moves when they should
Are you going to bring that up Thursday or just on the tram at everyone
Tram. I have an audience of one and she's already reading it
Walked over to the Frogner side. He's stood there so long that standing there is his position now. That's what makes it hard to watch
Tobias. That's the most you've said about a book since we started
I've been reading it
Starting the dean scene now. Thanks everyone for ruining it
Done. Not sleeping. Not sure which of us is worse at this
